![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119121/assets/8ffc97d4fc442503eb5b59e01f317cc7a77cf57d041e16807aa0645f962a5aeb.png)

Consider the vector field $F(x,y)$ shown above. Let $C$ be the path where the three-quarter circle is traversed from $A$ to $B.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
- ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$
- ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ gives the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along $C:$

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is true while statement II is false. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ assists the motion of the particle as it moves from $A$ to $B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119121/assets/c9805268d9f4984983c3cc5e2200a0c22d804bc67076a3505ad35471693c037b.png)

 
So, ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- Statement III is false. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ works against the motion of the particle as it moves from $B$ to $A.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119121/assets/dafb4d468e7711a804a5141301a02331bb5c7900f018a8ecdb6fd382bc05b799.png)

 
So, ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
